COMMON JUDGMENT
These two petitions are filed by the
Petitioners
U/s.166 of MV Act, seeking  compensation of 7,00,000/ and  16,00,000/ for the injuries sustained by  them in a same road traffic accident.

2 . The brief facts of the case are that  on 11052022 about 4.45 p.m., when the  Petitioners were travelling as passengers in  a Bus bearing No.KA10D4959 (herein after  called offending vehicle) and they were  sitting back right side 3 seater tyre  portion, at that time, near  Thippagondanahalli Dam, Taverekere Hobli,
 Bengaluru South Taluk, the driver of the  said bus drove the same with high speed, in  a rash and negligent manner and the right  back tyre burst the upper tyre foot board  broken and jumped upward.

Due to the impact,
 both Petitioners sustained grievous injuries  and immediately they were taken to Kenganur  hospital, Dasanapura Hobli, Bengaluru,
 wherein they have taken treatment as  inpatients and underwent surgery.

3. At the time of accident, the  Petitioner in MVC.3737/2022 was doing  Agriculture and earning 20,000/p.m.; the  SCCH.13 4 MVC.3737 & 3736/2022  Petitioner in MVC.3736/2022 was working as a  driver cum agriculture and earning 40,000/
 p.m.

2  suffering from permanent disability and  unable to lead normal life as earlier and  lost their earning capacity and income.
Further, they have spent huge amount towards  medical and other incidental expenses.

4. Petitioners claim that the accident  was due to negligence on the part of the  driver of the offending vehicle, as such,
 the Respondent No.1 and 2 being the owner  and insurer of the alleged vehicle are  jointly and severally liable to pay  compensation to the Petitioners.

5. In response to the petition notice,
 both the Respondents have appeared before  the court through their counsel and filed  the common written statement in both the  petitions.

6. Respondent No.1 RC owner filed his  written statement denying the negligence on  the part of driver of offending bus and  contended that the accident has occurred due  to the negligence of Petitioner.

This  Respondent has admitted that he is the RC  owner of the offending vehicle and the same  was insured with Respondent No.2 and the  policy was valid as on the date of accident  and the driver of offending bus was having  valid DL.
He has denied the other averments  of the petition.
It is said that the  compensation claimed is exaggerated and  without any basis and prayed for dismissal  of the petitions.

7. The Respondent No.2 - insurer in its  written statement has admitted the issuance  of policy to the offending vehicle and its  validity as on the date of accident and its  liability is subject to terms and conditions  of the policy.

It has contended that the  SCCH.13 6 MVC.3737 & 3736/2022  owner of the offending vehicle and the  concerned police have not complied the Girisha .N.G vs Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy .K.S on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/66769592/

 43. Liability:

Insurance company  denied its liability stating that the DL of  the driver of the offending vehicle was  lapsed as on the date of accident and the Girisha .N.G vs Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy .K.S on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/66769592/

In support of this contention,
 insurance company examined the RTO, Mandya  as RW1 and he has deposed that the driver
Purushothama
K.S. had DL to drive PSV bus  and badge, but his DL was lapsed and was not  renewed from 27122020 to 14062023.

Since  the accident has taken place on 11052022,
 as on the date of accident his DL was lapsed  one and half years ago.

RW2 official form  insurance company has produced permit  replacement endorsement issued by RTO,
 Mandya as per Ex.R.4.
According to this, he  had no valid permit to drive the vehicle.
According to Ex.R.4 permit was renewed for  the vehicle bearing No.KA10D4959.
In the  year 2014 in place of vehicle bearing No.KA  11A9592
. Again in the year 2015, permit  attached to vehicle bearing No.KA10D4959  was replaced to vehicle bearing No.KA11A  9592.
It is argued by the insurance company  that the offending vehicle had no permit as  on the date of accident.
It is not clear  SCCH.13 26 MVC.3737 & 3736/2022  from the Ex.R.4 endorsement whether the  offending vehicle had permit as on the date  of accident to run at that place.
No  evidence of RTO is adduced with regard to  permit.
However, it is proved that the DL  of the driver of offending vehicle was  lapsed as on the date of accident, which is  violation of insurance contract.
The driver  has got renewed his DL subsequent to the  accident.
It is clear that he was capable  to driving, but the DL was not properly  renewed.
44. In the present case admittedly  insurance covers the third party risk.
The  insurance policy is a contract executed  between the owner and the insurer.
In the  present case though the insurance was valid  as on the date of accident the owner allowed  the driver knowingly that his driving Girisha .N.G vs Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy .K.S

on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/66769592/
14  licence was lapsed.
It is the willful breach  of terms of contract of insurance.
45. Petitioners' counsel requested to  order for pay and recovery as it is the case  of injury to third party.
Insurance company  requeested to exonoerate their liability and  direct the owner to pay the compensation
as  he has appeared and contested the petition.

46 . Considering the available materials  on record and since it is the third party  liability, by following the decision of full  bench of Hon'ble Supreme Court the  Respondent No.2 insurance company i.e.
 insurer of the offending vehicle is directed  to pay the compensation and recover the same  from the owner i.e., Respondent No.1.
With  these observation I answer Issue No.2  partly in the affirmative.

The brief facts of the case are that  on 11052022 about 4.45 p.m., when the  Petitioners were travelling as passengers in  a Bus bearing No.KA10D4959 (herein after  called offending vehicle) and they were  sitting back right side 3 seater tyre  portion, at that time, near  Thippagondanahalli Dam, Taverekere Hobli,

Due to the impact,
 both Petitioners sustained grievous injuries  and immediately they were taken to Kenganur  hospital, Dasanapura Hobli, Bengaluru,
 wherein they have taken treatment as  inpatients and underwent surgery.
3. At the time of accident, the  Petitioner in MVC.3737/2022 was doing  Agriculture and earning 20,000/p.m.; the  SCCH.13 4 MVC.3737 & 3736/2022  Petitioner in MVC.3736/2022 was working as a  driver cum agriculture and earning 40,000/
 p.m.

4. Petitioners claim that the accident  was due to negligence on the part of the  driver of the offending vehicle, as such,
 the Respondent No.1 and 2 being the owner  and insurer of the alleged vehicle are  jointly and severally liable to pay  compensation to the Petitioners.
5. In response to the petition notice,
 both the Respondents have appeared before  the court through their counsel and filed  the common written statement in both the  petitions.
6. Respondent No.1 RC owner filed his  written statement denying the negligence on  the part of driver of offending bus and  contended that the accident has occurred due  to the negligence of Petitioner.
